preamble: The voiced dental/alveolar stop /d/ becomes the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] under the influence of a following palatal. In Hungarian this happens synchronically across morpheme boundaries: /d/ fuses with a following /j/ into a long palatal [ɟː] (full assimilation) and takes palatal place before a following gy /ɟ/ (partial assimilation).

examples.note: Full palatal assimilation: d + j fuse into a geminate palatal stop.
Partial assimilation: /d/ takes the palatal place of the following gy.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Hungarian phonology: palatal assimilation (adja [ɒɟːɒ], hadgyakorlat [hɒɟːɒkorlɒt]). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_phonology
